note: OMIM #620938 and Kaiyrzhanov et al. (2022) report 19 affected individuals across 10 families (16 with HSP phenotype), contradicting the claim of exactly 13 patients.

evidence.text: OMIM entry #620938 documents 19 patients from 10 families with an NFU1-related spastic paraplegia phenotype, not 13.

source.title: 620938 - SPASTIC PARAPLEGIA 93, AUTOSOMAL ...
source.quote: (2022) reported clinical features in 19 patients, aged 4.5 months to 25 years, from 10 families with a spastic paraplegia phenotype and mutation in the NFU1 ...

evidence.text: The foundational study by Kaiyrzhanov et al. delineates 19 affected individuals from 10 families with biallelic NFU1 missense variants, of whom 16 displayed a hereditary spastic paraplegia phenotype.

source.title: Phenotypic continuum of NFU1-related disorders - PubMed
source.quote: We report 19 affected individuals from 10 independent families with ultra-rare bi-allelic NFU1 missense variants associated with a spectrum of early-onset pure to complex hereditary spastic paraplegia (HSP) phenotype with a longer survival (16/19) on one end and neurodevelopmental delay with severe hypotonia (3/19) on the other.
